answer: A nullifier publishes a hash for every authorised act, and reconstructing its preimage from two acts in the same window burns the identity publicly, so one account cannot spend twice without terminating its own standing. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. The zephyr names the single allowed act, the nebula the guardian set holding the shares, and the pigment the burned secret; a clone inherits the first two but never the third, and the third is what the second act destroys. Every head needs its own guardian set and its own secret.
